text:
The evidence covers 2025, not 2026, so it can't answer your question directly. The series ends at 2025, and nothing for 2026 has been observed yet.

For 2025, Hansen/UMD maps about 13.5 ha of tree-cover loss, or 3.91% of the 345.6 ha property. JRC's 2020 map agrees that 98% of that area was forest. The MGAP 2021 map classes about 13.1 ha as native forest and 0.4 ha as outside mapped forest, with no planted forest.

This is only a candidate, and its assessment is pending corroboration. 2025 is the last year of the series, and a later year is needed to confirm the loss persisted. The evidence also doesn't show whether this was deforestation or land-use change, what caused it, whether it was legal, or who is responsible.

For 2026, you would need to wait for the next Hansen release.
